correctness.rationale: The Laplacian has nonzero eigenvalues p and p+q, yielding explicit L+ and (L+)^2 projectors. Two-edge deletion is a rank-two Woodbury correction on the constant-free subspace. The seven S_p x S_q edge-pair orbits are exhaustive; all seven rational damage formulas were inspected in COMPARISONS.md. Shifted variables u=p-3,v=q-2 give positive-coefficient exact difference numerators for A>B,C and B>D,E,F,G. The B-C sign is the concave quadratic F=-q^2+[p^2(p-3)+2]q+p^2(p-2)^2, with F(p,R_p)=1, F(p,R_p+1)=-p(p-1)(p-2). These are algebraic for all integer p,q, and independent rational Laplacian inverse tests corroborated small graphs. Post-deletion connectivity and omitted p=3 disjoint clique-edge orbit were checked.
residual_risks: Only simple complete split graphs p>=3,q>=2 with unit conductance and exactly two distinct deleted existing edges.

value.rationale: A complete ranking of worst and second-worst simultaneous two-link failures across a natural network family, including sharp cubic switching and exact multiplicities, addresses reliability patterns beyond generic Laplacian update computability.
residual_risks: Highly relevant 2024 weighted complete split graph article inaccessible in full; possible general resistance formula with hidden extremal conclusions.

final_claim: For unit-conductance complete split graphs K_p joined to an independent q-set, p>=3,q>=2, two cross edges sharing the independent-set endpoint uniquely maximize the two-edge Kirchhoff-index increase. Among strictly inferior pairs the runner-up switches from sharing a clique endpoint to disjoint cross edges when integer q passes R_p=p^3-3p^2+p+1, with no tie and exact orbit counts.
limitations: Only simple complete split graphs p>=3,q>=2 with unit conductance and exactly two distinct deleted existing edges.
